answer_1.quote: We compare UNIEVAL with several state-of-the-art evaluators... For compression and creation, we choose summarization and dialogue response generation... For transduction, we select data-to-text... UNIEVAL correlates well with human judgment on three typical generation tasks.

answer_2.quote: We adopt four meta-evaluation benchmarks for various NLG tasks to measure the correlation between UNIEVAL and human judgments... We compare UNIEVAL with several state-of-the-art evaluators. Notably, all the single-dimensional and unified evaluators are built on the same corpus. BERTScore is a similarity-based evaluator...

answer_3.quote: Using T5 as the backbone model, we first design specific rules for several commonly evaluated dimensions to construct pseudo data... For each input (x, y, c, q_i), evaluator should output "Yes" or "No" and calculate s_i as: s_i = P("Yes"|... ) / (P("Yes"|... ) + P("No"|... ))

answer_4.quote: SummEval provides human scores from four dimensions: fluency, coherence, consistency and relevance... Topical-Chat includes human scores from five dimensions: naturalness, coherence, engagingness, groundedness and understandability... We use summary-level Spearman and Kendall-Tau correlation to assess the performance of different evaluators for summarization.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators rated generated outputs on multiple dimensions such as fluency, coherence, consistency, relevance, naturalness, engagingness, groundedness, and understandability.
